newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH FOOD 11 PCT CHEAPER TWO YRS AFTER EU ENTRY.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH FOOD 11 PCT CHEAPER TWO YRS AFTER EU ENTRY.

text.p: Finnish food prices were 11.2
percent cheaper in October-November than two years ago before
Finland joined the European Union at the start of 1995, the
National Consumer Administration said in a statement on Monday.
"Food prices are now on average 11.2 percent cheaper than
two years ago before Finland became a member of the EU," it
said.
Most of the fall had occurred during the first year of EU
membership, it said, adding food prices had fallen on average
only by 0.1 percent in the year from the autumn of 1995.
The administration surveyed food retail prices at 153
outlets of nation-wide super market chains. The survey was
carried out in October-November. Price changes (pct):
vs late 1995 vs late 1994
Meat, meat products -5 -24
Bread, grain products -1 -14
Milk -2 -2
Cheese +2.5 -14
Fruit, fruit products +5 +4.3
Vegetables +16.5 +5.5
